title: Part Twenty-One: Constantine: Emperor, Pontifex, Patron

sections.brief: Diocletian's persecution (23-24 Feb 303, scriptures burned by the state), Galerius 311, Constantine proclaimed 306, Milvian Bridge 28 Oct 312 (Lactantius's dream c.315 vs Eusebius's later sky vision), Arch of 315 'instinctu divinitatis', Milan letter 13 June 313 (liberty for 'Christians and all others'), deathbed baptism 337 by Eusebius of Nicomedia, motive debate (Burckhardt, Brown, Leithart, Drake) left open. Figures: time

Sol on coins to 325/326; Sunday law 7 March 321 (civic rest; Christians met on Sunday by c.155, Justin); 25 December: history-of-religions vs calculation theories (McGowan, Hijmans); Mithras claims tested (rock birth, 25 Dec a modern proposal, zodiac not disciples; Justin's bread-and-cup comparison real); Pontifex Maximus held by emperors to Gratian (after Jan 379, Cameron), papal honorific only from the 15th c. Figures: compare (claim vs record)

Clergy immunity 313, bishops' courts 318/333, Lateran/St Peter's/Holy Sepulchre and endowments; Constantine's edict against Novatians, Valentinians, Marcionites, Paulians, Montanists (VC III.64-66: assemblies banned, buildings to the catholic church, books searched for); Arius's books to the flames; fifty Bibles; Constantius II, Julian; Cunctos populos 27 Feb 380, Constantinople 381, Gratian 382, laws of 391-392 and the enforcement debate; table of state book-burning orders 297/302-435. Figures: flow (patronage); compare (book-burning orders)
